summary: A 1923/1924 D-6 cupola lookout used as a camp from 1921, abandoned by the mid-1940s, restored starting 1982-83, and now a rentable Kootenai National Forest cabin.

facts.design: D-6 cupola cab, 12x12-ft wood frame with pyramidal roof and windowed cupola
facts.status_note: Abandoned for roughly three and a half decades mid-century before restoration; sources differ on exact abandonment and restoration-completion years

access.note: Reached by a 2.5-mile hike from Little Sutton Mountain trailhead; rented through Recreation.gov

visit.trail_note: 2.5-mile hike from the parking area at Little Sutton Mountain

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Kootenai National Forest (Rexford Ranger District)

events.note: First used as an unstructured camp lookout
D-6 cupola cab constructed; NHLR and firelookout.com both give 1924
Recreation.gov gives 1923 as the construction year, conflicting with the 1924 date on NHLR/firelookout.com
Recreation.gov: abandoned around 1944 after over 20 years of active fire-detection use
NHLR: abandoned for 35 years before the 1982 restoration, implying abandonment around 1947
NHLR and firelookout.com date the restoration to 1982 (NHLR) or 1983 (firelookout.com)
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, May 12, 2000, as US 345

evidence.supports: 35 years abandoned before 1982 restoration, 1924 D-6 cupola design, rarity of D-6 design nationwide
evidence.quote: After 35 years of abandonment, McGuire Mountain Lookout was restored in 1982 and placed in the rental system. The 1924 D-6 cupola lookout was a common design at the time it was constructed. The model was replaced by the L-4s, but a few of them remain as historic sites and only two or three are in fire service nationwide.

evidence.supports: built 1923, active over 20 years, abandoned around 1944, renovated 1983-1998
evidence.quote: McGuire Mountain Lookout was originally constructed in 1923 and was actively used as an observation point for detecting forest fires for over 20 years before it was abandoned around 1944. The structure was later renovated between 1983 and 1998 and is now available for rent for up to four people.

evidence.supports: location 14 miles SW of Eureka, 2.5-mile hike from Little Sutton Mountain parking
evidence.quote: McGuire Mountain is located approximately 14 miles southwest of Eureka. Access to the lookout requires a 2.5 mile hike from the parking area at Little Sutton Mountain.

evidence.supports: 12x12-ft wood-frame cabin, pyramidal roof, cupola with interior ladder, windows all around
evidence.quote: The lookout is a 12 x 12 foot wood-frame cabin with a pyramidal-shaped roof. On top of the roof there is a pyramidal-shaped cupola and a wooden ladder inside the cabin leading up to it. Windows completely surround the structure, providing a 360-degree view of the surrounding area.

evidence.supports: sleeps 4, wood stove, no electricity/water, locked with combination given to guests
evidence.quote: The rustic-style cabin is not wired for electricity. The main room is equipped with a modern wood stove... The lookout is secured with a cobination lock; please contact the Ranger District at (406) 296-2536 prior to arrival to confirm the combination.

evidence.supports: camp use from 1921, 1924 cabin built, restored 1983, listed on NHLR
evidence.quote: First used as a camp in 1921, the present D-6 cupola cabin was constructed in 1924. After being abandoned for several decades, the cabin was restored in 1983 and placed on the Recreation Rental program. It is listed on the National Historic Lookout Register.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and firelookout.com give 1924; Recreation.gov gives 1923. Story and events list both rather than picking one, since neither source is clearly authoritative over the other.

NHLR's '35 years of abandonment before 1982' implies abandonment around 1947; Recreation.gov says abandoned around 1944 and renovated 1983-1998. The two are not fully reconcilable from the text available, so both are reported with attribution rather than merged into one timeline.

notes_for_editor: The brief flagged a register-number conflict ('They share a register number') but none of the three sources checked here show a shared/duplicate NHLR number; US 345 appears specific to McGuire on both NHLR and the firelookout.org list. That conflict may concern a source not checked in this pass. No source gives a specific fire credited to this lookout, or the exact date staffing began. Fact-check 2026-10-04: the draft's sentence on the 1923/1924 build-year split misattributed the dates, crediting Recreation.gov with the 1924 figure (it actually gives 1923, per source 2) and leaving firelookout.com unnamed as one of the two sources giving 1924; corrected. The physical-description sentence (pyramidal roof, cupola, interior ladder) cited only sources 1 and 3, but that detail comes from source 2's quote, so source 2 was added to the citation. A sentence claiming the lookout sat on 'Lincoln National Forest' land before the area became Kootenai National Forest was removed -- no source (and no real Forest Service unit near Eureka, MT) supports that name; it appears to be a mix-up with 'Lincoln Mountain,' which is actually part of the unrelated Garnet Mountain story in this same batch.
